First of all, I really do not understand how a person can be late to a class by at least 10 minutes every single class. It's not only surprising but also super disrespectful towards the students. We arrive on time and wait for the teacher, and for what? 

It feels like there is a lack of attention to the lecture, and this is being reflected in the students, decreasing our enthusiasm. I get that teachers can be busy with their labs, but that does not change their responsibility towards the class. The slides are so poorly designed, and it feels like there is not enough preparation before class. 

The main way we followed the lecture, with students presenting alone, is quite mismanaged and does not really help students learn the material. I think she chose this way because she did not want to deal with teaching.

About the midterm, where a question was asked that was literally not in our responsibilities, copy pasted the title of a random paper. Then, when we confronted her, she said, "In the future, people are going to try to deceive you." So??? Does that give you the right to do it in a midterm? No, I don't think so. I think she forgot that we were not responsible for that paper. On top of that, she probably said she was going to upload the results 2 times and did not. I just do not get it. 

Lastly, her use of English leads to explanations that can be incorrect or misleading. I believe instructors are expected to meet a certain level of proficiency, but in this case, it affects how we understand the material. If such requirements already exist, they may need to place more emphasis on speaking clarity, since it directly impacts comprehension. In biology, a single word can change the meaning of a sentence, so unclear explanations can lead to misunderstandings.

In conclusion, while the course itself was interesting, the instructor did not manage it effectively.
